findings.title: Initialization function without `initializer` modifier
findings.description: The function appears to be an initialization function but does not use the `initializer` or `reinitializer` modifier. This means it can be called multiple times, potentially allowing an attacker to re-initialize the contract and take ownership.
findings.recommendation: Add the `initializer` modifier from OpenZeppelin's `Initializable` contract to ensure it can only be called once.

findings.recommendation: Never allow user-controlled addresses as delegatecall targets. Use a whitelist of approved implementation addresses or restrict to owner-set immutable addresses.

findings.title: State variable set in constructor of upgradeable contract
findings.description: The constructor of this upgradeable contract sets state variables. In a proxy pattern, the constructor runs in the context of the implementation contract, not the proxy. These values will NOT be available when the proxy delegates calls to this implementation.
findings.recommendation: Move state initialization to the `initialize()` function. The constructor should only call `_disableInitializers()`. Use `immutable` for values that truly need to be set at deploy time (they are stored in bytecode, not storage).

An attacker could re-enter `swapExactBNBForTokensAndSupply` during `swapExactTokensForTokensAndSupplyAtSupportingFee`'s external call to manipulate shared state.
findings.recommendation: Apply `nonReentrant` to both functions, or ensure the CEI pattern is followed with state updates before external calls in both functions.

An attacker could re-enter `swapTokensForExactBNBAndSupply` during `swapBNBForExactTokensAndRepay`'s external call to manipulate shared state.
findings.recommendation: Apply `nonReentrant` to both functions, or ensure the CEI pattern is followed with state updates before external calls in both functions.

findings.title: Potential cross-function reentrancy: `_calculateScore` and `calculateAPR`
findings.description: Functions `_calculateScore` (has external call) and `calculateAPR` both modify shared state variables: balanceOfAccount, borrow, capital, exchangeRate, supply, vToken. findings.recommendation: Apply `nonReentrant` to both functions, or ensure the CEI pattern is followed with state updates before external calls in both functions.

findings.title: Setter `setMaxTokensDistributionSpeed` lacks bounds validation
findings.description: The function `setMaxTokensDistributionSpeed` sets a critical parameter but does not validate input bounds. An owner could set the value to an extreme (e.g., 100% fee) to extract user funds.
findings.recommendation: Add upper/lower bound checks. For fees, enforce a maximum (e.g., `require(fee <= MAX_FEE)`). Emit events on changes for off-chain monitoring.

findings.title: Potential cross-function reentrancy: `mintVAI` and `repayVAIFresh`
findings.description: Functions `mintVAI` (has external call) and `repayVAIFresh` both modify shared state variables: _vai, pastVAIInterest. An attacker could re-enter `repayVAIFresh` during `mintVAI`'s external call to manipulate shared state.
findings.recommendation: Apply `nonReentrant` to both functions, or ensure the CEI pattern is followed with state updates before external calls in both functions.

findings.title: CEI violation in `mintVAI`: state change after external call
findings.description: In function `mintVAI`, a state variable is modified after an external call. This violates the Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern and can allow an attacker to re-enter the function before the state update completes.
findings.recommendation: Move all state changes before external calls (follow the CEI pattern). Alternatively, add a `nonReentrant` modifier from OpenZeppelin's ReentrancyGuard.

findings.recommendation: Add upper/lower bound checks. For fees, enforce a maximum (e.g., `require(fee <= MAX_FEE)`). Emit events on changes for off-chain monitoring.

findings.title: Potential cross-function reentrancy: `_reduceReservesFresh` and `accrueInterest`
findings.description: Functions `_reduceReservesFresh` (has external call) and `accrueInterest` both modify shared state variables: totalReserves. An attacker could re-enter `accrueInterest` during `_reduceReservesFresh`'s external call to manipulate shared state.
findings.recommendation: Apply `nonReentrant` to both functions, or ensure the CEI pattern is followed with state updates before external calls in both functions.

findings.title: Potential cross-function reentrancy: `_reduceReservesFresh` and `_addReservesFresh`

findings.recommendation: Apply `nonReentrant` to both functions, or ensure the CEI pattern is followed with state updates before external calls in both functions.

findings.title: Hardcoded decimal assumption (10^18)
findings.description: The contract uses a hardcoded decimal value of 10^18 near oracle-related code. Not all Chainlink feeds use 8 decimals (e.g., ETH/USD uses 8, but some feeds use 18). Hardcoding decimals can cause incorrect price scaling.
findings.recommendation: Query the oracle's `decimals()` function dynamically, or document the assumption clearly and validate it in the constructor.

findings.title: Missing zero-address check for `account` in constructor
findings.description: The constructor accepts address parameter `account` but does not validate that it is not the zero address. Accidentally passing address(0) could brick the contract.
findings.recommendation: Add `require(account != address(0), "zero address");` or use a custom error for gas efficiency.

findings.title: Unsafe downcast to `uint96`
findings.description: The value `totalSupply` is cast to `uint96` without bounds checking. If the value exceeds the maximum for `uint96` (2^96 - 1), it will silently truncate, leading to incorrect values.
findings.recommendation: Use OpenZeppelin's SafeCast library: `value.toUint96()` which reverts on overflow. Alternatively, add an explicit bounds check.

findings.title: Read-only reentrancy risk: `doTransferIn` may return stale data
findings.description: View function `doTransferIn` reads balance/share state that is also modified by `_reduceReservesFresh` (which has external calls). If `_reduceReservesFresh` makes an external call before updating state, a callback could invoke `doTransferIn` and get stale values. This is exploitable if other protocols rely on this view function.
findings.recommendation: Ensure state is updated before external calls in `_reduceReservesFresh`. If this view function is used by external protocols for pricing, consider adding reentrancy protection.

findings.title: Unsigned to signed integer conversion
findings.description: Converting an unsigned integer to a signed type can produce a negative value if the unsigned value exceeds the signed type's maximum (e.g., uint256 > type(int256).max). In Solidity 0.8+, this reverts; in earlier versions, it wraps.
findings.recommendation: Validate that the value fits in the target signed type before casting. Use SafeCast for safe conversions.

findings.recommendation: Use OpenZeppelin's `Ownable2Step` which requires the new owner to call `acceptOwnership()`, preventing accidental transfers to wrong addresses.

findings.title: Immutable variable `newBorrower` in upgradeable contract
findings.description: The immutable variable `newBorrower` is stored in the implementation contract's bytecode. This is safe and gas-efficient, but the value will be determined when the implementation is deployed and cannot be changed through proxy upgrades.
findings.recommendation: Ensure the immutable value is correct for all proxies that will use this implementation. If different proxies need different values, use a regular state variable set in `initialize()` instead.
